title: Mirrored Meteor and Milky Way
explanation:
# Rewritten for General Audience

A brilliant Perseid meteor blazed across the night sky above Spain's La Palma observatory, its colorful trail streaking past the cloudy, starlit band of our Milky Way galaxy. In the foreground, the massive 23-meter mirror of a cutting-edge telescope—made up of nearly 200 hexagonal segments—caught not just distant cosmic explosions from galaxies billions of light-years away, but also reflected this fleeting space rock burning up in Earth's atmosphere, capturing two wonders of the universe in a single frame.
